key_insight: Adding Tikhonov regularization to PINNs makes terminal-state optimal control for parabolic PDEs well-posed and steers the learned control toward the minimum-energy solution.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more stable and physically meaningful neural solver for distributed control tasks in heat-transfer and fluid-like systems where many controls can achieve the same terminal target.
method: PINNs enforce the PDE dynamics, boundary/initial conditions, and terminal-state objective.
A Tikhonov term penalizes control energy to resolve non-uniqueness and smooth the control.
Theory gives a consistency result plus an error bound tied to training residuals and the regularization weight.
evidence_signal: Experiments on the linear heat equation and nonlinear Burgers' equation show accurate terminal-state tracking with lower-energy, smoother controls than unregularized PINN baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful tuning of the regularization parameter and sufficient residual/quadrature accuracy; overly small or large regularization can hurt either stability or target tracking.
paper_title: Tikhonov-Regularized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Terminal-State Distributed Optimal Control of Parabolic Partial Differential Equations
